paper_claims.claim: NowWAM removes the separate future visual target and applies native denoising directly to the current visual stream, achieving 87.7% on LIBERO-Plus with FLUX2-Klein-4B and 87.8% with Z-Image-6B.

Controlled ablation shows past (t-16, 83.80%), future (t+16, 82.89%), and far future (t+32, 83.70%) auxiliary targets perform comparably, proving future prediction is not uniquely privileged for generative adaptation.

Restricting training to the clean endpoint (sigma=0) drops LIBERO-Plus success from 84.97% to 77.48%, and removing visual denoising loss drops it to 78.73%, demonstrating that coupling to the denoising trajectory is the true driver of robustness.
NowWAM halves training visual tokens from 784 to 392, reducing per-step training time from 2.85s to 1.63s (1.8x speedup) and peak GPU memory from 78.9 GiB to 74.3 GiB on 2xH200.
On Standard LIBERO, NowWAM reaches 98.4% average success (Spatial 99.5%, Object 100.0%), and on RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop 100-shot, reaches 64.9% (vs Fast-WAM 56.0%, DIAL 58.3%).
On LIBERO-Plus under challenging viewpoint perturbations, NowWAM achieves 88.6%, significantly outperforming ImageWAM (77.7%), pi0.5 (78.4%), and Fast-WAM (15.5%).
